metrics.name: onset_repetitions
metrics.threshold: extra fragment(s) before the word, +time at this boundary

metrics.name: fragment_vs_word_onset_similarity
metrics.threshold: MFCC cosine > 0.80 = the same onset repeated

regions.explanation: At 0.91s, the onset of “and” is repeated 2 time(s) before the word is completed (fragment-to-onset spectral similarity 0.97). Repeated onsets before the word is completed fragment it and interrupt the speech rhythm. Fix: Begin the word once, deliberately; a short breath before it helps.

regions.text: earlier today have led me to change those plans. Today is a
regions.explanation: From 7.24s to 16.14s (“earlier today have led me to change those plans. Today is a”), articulation rate slowed to 2.49 syll/s against 4.04 syll/s in the reference (-38%); that is 1.5× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Stretched words without matching emphasis read as hesitation and dilute the rhythm of the phrase; the audience's attention drifts between content words. Fix: Tighten these words to the reference pace; keep length only on the stressed word.

regions.text: tragedy of the shuttle Challenger. We
regions.explanation: From 20.94s to 23.28s (“tragedy of the shuttle Challenger. We”), loudness relative to the speaker's own level fell 8.3 dB below the reference, bottoming out 11.0 dB down; that is 1.7× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. The loudness falls away across the phrase, so its final words - often the payoff - drop toward the noise floor of the room. Fix: Support the breath through the end of the phrase; the last words need the same energy as the first.

metrics.name: pause_length
metrics.threshold: >= 0.3 s longer than reference, mid-phrase (no punctuation)

regions.explanation: At 24.48s, between “this” and “pain”, a 1.48 s silence replaced the reference's 0 ms pause. A long silence where the reference has none - especially mid-phrase - breaks the syntactic unit and signals lost place rather than deliberate emphasis. Fix: Keep this phrase in one breath; pause at the punctuation instead.

regions.text: of the people of our country. This is truly
regions.explanation: From 27.08s to 28.80s (“of the people of our country. This is truly”), articulation rate was 6.98 syll/s against 4.69 syll/s in the reference (+49%); that is 1.3× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Faster articulation compresses the stressed syllables and the micro-pauses listeners use to segment phrases, so key words lose emphasis and comprehension drops. Fix: Slow to the reference pace here and let the pauses between clauses breathe.

regions.text: loss as a nation together. For the families of the
regions.explanation: From 72.72s to 76.12s (“loss as a nation together. For the families of the”), the share of energy above 2 kHz dropped to 2.6% from 10.6% (-75%); that is 2.0× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Energy above 2 kHz carries consonant bursts and fricatives (t, k, s, f); losing it blurs word boundaries and makes the speech sound muffled even at normal volume. Fix: Open the mouth more and finish final consonants crisply.

metrics.name: held_steady_voicing
metrics.threshold: steady pitch + unchanging spectrum >= 140 ms longer than reference

regions.explanation: At 84.62s, between “you” and “so”, a 10 ms held vowel (“uh”/“um”) appears where the reference holds 30 ms, adding 710 ms at this word boundary. A held, unchanging vowel that maps to no word in the transcript is a filled pause; listeners hear it as hesitation, and judges penalise it under fluency. Fix: Replace the filler with silence - a clean pause sounds deliberate.
